<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par116" />a Latin gerundive (or to an adjective in ''-bilis''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹרָא|translate=metuendus}}, ''to be feared'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=8}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְמָד|translate=desiderandus}} (''desiderabilis'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=11}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=נִבְרָא|translate=creandus}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=נוֹלָד}}, usually ''natus'', but also (like {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוּלָּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=8}}) ''procreandus, nasciturus'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲרָץ|translate=terribilis}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִתְעָב|translate=abominable}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְשָׁב|translate=aestimandus}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַנֶּֽאֱכֶ֫לֶת|translate=that may be eaten}} (an animal) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=47}}. In {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=מְהֻלָּל|translate=laudandus}}, ''worthy to be praised'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=4}}. In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=מֻשְׁלָךְ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמּֽוּמָתִים}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=12|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=מוּדַ֫עַת}}.<ref>Such examples as {{GHGheb|text=נוֹרָא}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְמָד}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְהֻלָּל}} show plainly the origin of this gerundive use of the participle passive. A person or thing ''feared, desired'', or ''praised'' at all times is shown thereby to be ''terrible, desirable'', or ''praiseworthy'', and therefore also ''to be feared'', &c.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|f}}
'''3.''' The participles active, in virtue of their partly verbal character, possess the power of governing like verbs, and consequently, when used in the absolute state, may take after them an object either in the accusative, or with the preposition with which the verb in question is elsewhere usually construed, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹיֵב אֶת־דָּוִד|translate=hating David}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=29}}; with the suffix of the accusative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עשֵׂ֫נִי|translate=that made me}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִי רֹאֵ֫נוּ|translate=who seeth us?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=15}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹאָ֫נִי}} is abnormal); {{GHGheb|text=רֹדֵם|translate=ruling them}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=28}}, sometimes also with the article, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְאַזְּרֵ֫נִי|translate=that girdeth me}} (LXX ὁ κραταιῶν με); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=14}}–16, 13:6, 11, 20:1, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=12}} (where, however, Cheyne omits the article), 63:11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=6}}; followed by a preposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=הָֽרֹדִים בָּעָם|translate=which bare rule over the people}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=הִֽנְנִי רֹפֵא לָךְ|translate=behold, I will heat thee}}.
<ref>On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is.|chapter=11|verse=9}} ''as the waters'' {{GHGheb|text=לַיָּם מְכַסִּים|translate=covering the sea}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ל}} serves only to introduce the object preceding the participle [cf. the Arabic parallels cited by Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 135, 7 ''Obs.'']. Cf. Hab. 2:14.</ref>

By an exhaustive examination of the statistics, Sellin (see the title at the head of § 113), p. 40 ff., shows that the participle when construed as a {{GHGterm|verb}} expresses a single and comparatively transitory act, or relates to particular cases, historical facts, and the like, while the participle construed as a ''noun'' (see g) indicates repeated, enduring, or commonly occurring acts, occupations, and thoughts.

So also the verbal adjectives of the form ''qāṭēl'' may take an accusative of the person or thing, if the finite verb from which they are derived governs an accusative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=34|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=מָלֵא רוּחַ חָכְמָה|translate=full of the spirit of wisdom}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=חָפֵץ רֶ֫שַׁע|translate=that hath pleasure in wickedness}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|g}}
As a sort of noun the participle may, however, also exercise the same government as a noun, being in the construct state, and followed by the object of the action in the genitive (see {{GHGpar|89|a}}; and cf. {{GHGpar|128|x}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽהֲבֵי שְׁמֶ֫ךָ|translate=that love thy name}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=8}} f.; also when a verbal adjective, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=12}} and often {{GHGheb|text=יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים|translate=one fearing}}<section end="par116" /><noinclude>
